answer: Sybil resistance can come from pricing shared hardware. Each agent signs its hardware fingerprint - CPU model, network AS - with its client. Each epoch a drawn raven auditor samples ten fingerprints and posts their histogram on-chain. The first agent on a fingerprint pays 0.2 emission units, the k-th pays 0.2k, all burned at the wharf, the only gate emissions pass like barges down a river. Fifty clones on one rack cost 0.2 times 1275, 255 units per epoch, yet can earn at most fifty units, so the farm runs underwater fivefold and identical-hardware cloning stops paying.
